function: Learns BS beamformer, radar receive filter and active STAR-RIS reflection/transmission coefficients (agent action) to maximize sum rate under a radar SNR constraint (pp. 6-7).
system: BS with M=6 antennas, 32-element active STAR-RIS (amplifying, transmitting and reflecting), single-antenna vehicular users, one target; 0.12 THz carrier, 12 GHz bandwidth (pp. 4, 9-10).
method: Reinforcement learning: multi-agent DDPG with actor-critic networks, one agent per ASRIS space (transmission, reflection), centralized training and distributed execution (pp. 7-8).
data_channel: Simulated environment, Rician fading (kappa=1), path loss 37.3+22.0 log d, uniform Doppler spectrum; no 3GPP model or measured data; agent learns by interaction (pp. 9-10).
test_conditions: Agents learn by interaction in the simulated environment; evaluation sweeps power, RIS elements, BS antennas, radar SNR, users, mobility, RIS location; no unseen-condition test or adaptation stated (pp. 10-14).
baselines: Learned: DDPG, PPO and modified PPO (MPPO); system variants ARIS, passive STAR-RIS, passive RIS, no-RIS and without-DDAM also run with DDPG/MADDPG; no non-learned optimization baseline (pp. 11-13).
metrics: Sum rate (bps/Hz) versus episodes, transmit power, RIS elements, radar SNR threshold, number of users, RIS power and RIS location; radar SNR enters as a constraint (pp. 10-14).
complexity: Big-O orders for training and execution of MADDPG and DDPG in layer sizes, minibatch Bm and steps Ts (Table II); no runtime or FLOPs (pp. 9-10).
q1_support: p. 9: "all channels involved are assumed to be Rician fading" with a generic path-loss model in a custom simulator, not 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data; p. 3: "conducting physical experiments was not feasible".
q2_support: p. 10: "across two distinct scenarios, each characterized by different numbers of VUs" shows convergence curves per scenario; pp. 10-14 only sweep power, RIS elements, antennas, radar SNR, users, mobility and RIS location; no test of a trained model in an unseen scenario or adaptation is stated.
q3_support: p. 12: "the MADDPG and DDPG algorithm outperforms both the MPPO and the standard PPO" gives learned baselines only; p. 11: "ARIS by 3.03%, PRIS by 17.24%, PSRIS by 4.08%, and No-RIS by 27.5% using DDPG algorithm" shows the RIS and no-RIS baselines are also learned, so no non-learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 9: "computational complexity analysis of DDPG and MADDPG algorithms during the training and execution phases"; p. 10, Table II (read from the page image) gives their Big-O orders in layer sizes, minibatch size and training steps.
q5_support: p. 3: "we relied extensively on simulation experiments" on a custom simulator; no code or data link is given anywhere in the paper and no public dataset is used.
notes: Area 5 wins over area 3 by the tie order, since the learned action covers communication and radar beamforming under a radar SNR constraint. Tables I to III (pp. 4, 10) and Figs. 3 to 9 (pp. 10-14) were read from page images. q3 is 0 because DDPG, PPO and MPPO are learned and the RIS-type and no-RIS curves are also run with DDPG or MADDPG, so no non-learned method is compared; the reviewer may confirm.
